gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a variable ND is two polarizing layers rotated against each other, so near its darkest setting it shows an X-shaped dark pattern, worse on wide lenses. Makers cap the range for that reason: K&F's ND2-32 stops at 5 stops 'with reduced "X" effect', and Kenko advises staying at ND128 or below at 24mm. A 1–5 stop VND is therefore about 1 stop short of 1/50 s at f/2.8 in full sun at ISO 100.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches. Its saved chat has no results and no cited pages, so there was no rival page to compare against. The only comparison is ChatGPT's own answer, which calls a variable ND 'especially useful for video' without saying it is two polarizers, without mentioning the X pattern near maximum density or on wide lenses, and without saying that makers limit VND range (K&F 1–5 stops) for this reason.
decides: This settles whether a VND alone works. On lenses of about 24mm and longer with a moderate need (up to about 5 stops), the listed K&F ND2-32 True Color VND (67mm or 77mm) works: its 1–5 stop cap keeps it out of the worst-X zone. Wide-open daylight video at a 180° shutter needs about 6 stops at f/2.8 (about 7.3 at f/1.8, for example on the listed Meike 85mm F1.8), which is more than the ND2-32 gives. Those shoppers need a fixed ND (K&F's own advice) or a stronger VND kept at ND128 or below on wide lenses (Kenko's limit at 24mm). Ask the shopper's focal length and aperture before recommending the K&F VND.

findings.label: How a variable ND works and why the X pattern appears
findings.value: "combines two polarizing films to achieve step-less light reduction"; "The occurrence of X-pattern is in principle unavoidable for all variable ND systems that use polarizing films"
findings.source_title: Characteristics of Creation Variable ND using polarizing film (Marumi, 2022-02-01)
findings.note: Marumi also says the light reduction 'changes gently from the Min. position and rapidly as it approaches the Max. position', and recommends 'a focal length of 24 mm or more' to reduce the X pattern.

findings.label: Why the X pattern is worse at the frame edges and on wide lenses
findings.value: "Light reaching the edges of the frame passes through the filter at a different angle compared with light near the center"; a VND clean at 50mm may show an obvious X at 16mm
findings.source_title: Variable ND Filter X Pattern: Causes & How to Fix It (K&F Concept, 2026-08-11)
findings.note: K&F: 'There is no universal focal-length limit.' For stronger reduction it recommends a fixed ND: 'A fixed ND provides consistent light reduction without pushing the VND into its most extreme polarization position.' The article says the K&F ND2-32 uses 'a controlled 1-to-5-stop adjustment range'.

findings.label: Usable density at 24mm
findings.value: ND2.5 to ND128 (about 1.3–7 stops) at 24mm, out of a rated ND2.5–1000 (1.6–10 stops)
findings.note: Kenko recommends 'to use only up to ND128' at 24mm and says pushing toward ND1000 raises the chance of 'X-shape pattern and color shift'. It claims 'a unique manufacturing method to minimize X-shape pattern'. Price not checked.

findings.label: ND needed for 180° shutter video in full sun
findings.value: about 6 stops (ND64) at f/2.8, ISO 100, 1/50 s; about 7.3 stops at f/1.8
findings.note: Sunny 16 gives f/16 at 1/100 s for ISO 100 in direct sun. Going from f/16 to f/2.8 adds 5 stops, so 1/3200 s. Going from 1/3200 to 1/50 is 64×, which is 6 stops. f/2.8 to f/1.8 adds about 1.3 stops. A 5-stop ND2-32 at maximum leaves the shutter at 1/100 s with f/2.8 and ISO 100. Cameras with a higher base ISO need more ND.
